newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK protesters urge China to put pressure on Japan.
newsitem.headline: HK protesters urge China to put pressure on Japan.

text.p: A Hong Kong protest group urged China on Thursday to put pressure on Tokyo to destroy all symbols of Japanese sovereignty on a disputed East China Sea archipelago and to remove its navy from the surrounding waters.

"The alliance believes China ought to use stronger foreign action to force the Japanese government to destroy all structures on the Diaoyus and to get its navy out of surrounding waters," the Hong Kong Universal Alliance for Protection of the Diaoyu Islands said in a statement.

The alliance issued the statement after the leader of another Hong Kong group, David Chan, drowned on Thursday when he and four other activists leapt off a protest ship into the East China Sea to challenge Japan's claims to the isles.
"The alliance urges all Hong Kong people to turn their sorrow into strength and to pick up the baton of Chan's mission to continue protecting the Diaoyus," it said.
But the alliance cautioned that the movement to protect the isles should proceed in a cool and safe manner.

Chan's drowning was the first death in almost two months of protests to sweep through Hong Kong, China, Taiwan and Macau since Japanese rightists built a lighthouse and raised Japanese flags on the islands.
Japan has claimed sovereign rights to the islands and refused to acknowledge that the dispute is still open for discussion with China.

Tokyo's claim to what it calls the Senkaku Islands dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries, referring to them as the Diaoyu Isles.
